head: 690c2125da360da8a5e73aa461a10e7333b7daa9
classification_reasons: Spec is tight: the intent's three open questions are each answered with the intent's own proposal, the one flagged concern (version bump) is now closed by panel decision 1 (keep 0.1.0, with the reason that tests/test_smoke.py asserts 0.1.0 and a fix-type diff may not edit it), and acceptance is measurable (four named tests, the three commands, pip install -e . with a clean tree, the owner's Windows check).

Blast radius is not small: it rebuilds the opener every download goes through, changes packaging (a new [tool.setuptools] table, a new Windows-only runtime dependency), and leaves two guardrail lines (CLAUDE.md Setup, sdlc.yaml commands.setup line 62) for the owner to change in a set order.

No existing test covers the real opener (the suite drives the layer through stub fetches), so its behaviour rests on the new tests alone; the Windows tzdata outcome has no CI coverage and is checked by the owner at the deploy gate.
attempted: Intent: outcome 1 maps to R1-R5, outcome 2 to R6-R8, outcome 3 to R9-R13; the Constraints (proxy support, offline tests, CI unchanged, guardrail lines for the owner only, guardrail PR after the packaging fix) each appear in spec or plan. R7 widens the datetime refusal to clear_cache, which has the same TypeError (cache.py:146-147, compared at :153); that follows from the intent's fix rather than adding scope.

Spec and plan: every requirement has a step; the only flagged concern is closed with a decision ('decided (by panel #1)'), and plan.md 'Options not taken' agrees (version kept at 0.1.0). The only change since the previous review (a9f4798) is that closing in spec.md plus panel and evidence files; the HEAD diff touches only the change folder. Files that change match the intent's affected list.

Proof: design phase, so there are no toolchain logs to expect. plan.md Proof names four tests, marked as still to be written in step 1. The prototype has three of them; the plan adds the clear_cache test and the parameter type hints the prototype lacks.

Blast radius: no risk-list item (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config; deploy.action none); risk-hits returned none. No guardrail file is in the diff. Callers checked by grep: urllib_fetch (loader.py:82 default, __main__.py:26); parse_date (make_request at params.py:99-100, clear_cache at cache.py:146-147). The CLI passes argparse strings and loader/CLI pass now.date() only as `today`, which parse_date never sees. No existing test passes a datetime bound. app/ holds only the app and app.data packages, so the packages list is complete.

Policies: the tzdata dependency has its Risks line (coding-standards rule 5, security-baseline rule 6); TLS context untouched; no live call by a run (security-baseline rule 7); the new message says what happened and what to pass (ux rule 4); data-conventions correctly judged not applicable.

Tests: redirect test, on main: HTTPRedirectHandler follows the Location to the stubbed target (HTTPHandler.http_open or _HTTPSHandler.https_open, both patched at class level, looked up at call time by _call_chain) until loop detection, so `opened == [origin]` fails on Python 3.12 for 301/302/303/307/308. With the fix, HTTPErrorProcessor.https_response -> parent.error('http') -> no http_error_3xx handler -> HTTPDefaultErrorHandler raises HTTPError, which urllib_fetch turns into HttpResponse(status); dict(email.message.Message) works for the headers. Scheme test: on main http/ftp to loopback give a connection-refused URLError that does not match 'unknown url type', and file:// reads the file, so all three fail; with the fix UnknownHandler raises before any socket opens, even when http_proxy/ftp_proxy are set (ProxyHandler returns None for a same-type proxy, or re-opens as http, which UnknownHandler then refuses). Datetime test: comparing a datetime with a date raises TypeError on main for all six combinations (the intent's prototype count of 19 = 10 + 3 + 6 agrees). clear_cache test writes a day file first, so on main it hits the comparison at cache.py:153. Fix-type: no existing test changes; tests/test_smoke.py stays untouched because the version is kept.
Skip markers: not checked at design (ratchets runs at build and test).

Claims against today's code: http.py:78 `_OPENER = urllib.request.build_opener(_HTTPSHandler())` - true; CONNECT_TIMEOUT/READ_TIMEOUT in _HTTPSConnection and MAX_BODY_BYTES in _read - true; urllib_fetch catches HTTPError into HttpResponse - true; with_retries returns any status < 500 other than 418/429 (http.py:114) - true; OSError in TRANSIENT_ERRORS, so a URLError would be retried - true, and listed as a risk; vision.py:60 'Vision refused (HTTP ...)' and rest.py:68 'REST refused (HTTP ...)' - true; parse_date at params.py:77 returns any date unchanged - true; cached_days(root, market, symbol, interval, days) in tests/binance_stub.py:30 - true; test_cache_info_and_clear_touch_only_day_files at test_data.py:292 - true; sdlc.yaml:62 `setup: "python -m pip install pytest ruff polars"` - true; pyproject.toml has dependencies ['polars>=1.0'] and no [tool.setuptools] or [build-system] table - true; tests/test_smoke.py:5 asserts '0.1.0' and REVIEW.md:23-24 has the fix-type test rule (both cited by the panel decision) - true. Proxy claim (R5): for an https URL, ProxyHandler.proxy_open sets a tunnel and returns None, so _HTTPSHandler opens it on _HTTPSConnection and the timeouts still apply - consistent with urllib. No docs/decisions/ exists, and the spec cites no decision.
Drive: not applicable at design (commands.drive is empty).
